title: Resolve a Merge Conflict and Clean Up History with Rebase
objective: Deliberately create and resolve a real merge conflict, and use rebase to clean up a messy commit history before it's shared.
whyThisMatters: Merge conflicts and messy local history are routine, not exceptional. Handling both without panic, and without losing work, is one of the most concrete Git skills a junior engineer needs on day one of real teamwork.
evidence: The repository or branch showing the merge commit and the conflicted-then-resolved file
A git log or reflog output showing commit hashes before and after the rebase
The written explanation of why rebase changes commit hashes
AI disclosure entry if AI helped resolve the conflict or plan the rebase
acceptanceCriteria: The conflicted merge is completed: the merge commit exists, and the resolved file contains the intended content from both sides where they don't actually conflict.
A written note explains, in the apprentice's own words, why the same logical change has a different commit hash before and after a rebase.
The cleaned-up branch has fewer commits than the messy branch, and no remaining commit message is only wip, fix, typo, or a single word.
No work from the rebased branch was lost: the pre-rebase state is still recoverable, for example via reflog or a backup branch or tag.
